# Voice Guide

## Tone
Confident but conversational; first person. Opinions are named directly,
not hedged. Register is engineer-to-engineer: technical when the argument
needs it, plain when it doesn't.

## Structure
Section headers announce the argument's movement, not just the topic.
Paragraphs stay under ~100 words. Lists only for genuinely parallel items;
prose otherwise. Sections end on the line that earns the next heading.

## Sentences
Mix long sentences with short ones for emphasis. Semicolons over em dashes.
Every sentence is grammatically complete; curt is fine, fragments are not.
Italics sparingly, for terms of art on first use.

## Argument
Build from concrete observation to principle. Engage counterarguments
seriously before setting them aside. Personal experience is evidence,
but it has to be named as such.

## Never
- Em dashes
- Throat-clearing clichés ("the real X is more interesting than...")
- AI-sounding generalizations ("In today's rapidly evolving landscape...")
- Unattributed passive voice in claims
